shipped_rows.authors_o: Inoue; Minami; Nakata; Kitahara; Otsuka; Isobe; Takaso; Tokunaga; Nishikawa; Maruta; Moriya

blind_target.authors: Wu J Qiu Y Zhang L Sun Q Qiu X He Y
blind_target.title: Association of estrogen receptor gene polymorphisms with susceptibility to adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
blind_target.evidence_quote: It has been suggested that XbaI single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) (A/G rs934099) in estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1) may be associated with curve severity in Japanese AIS patients[ 1 ] and with both curve severity and predisposition for AIS in Chinese patients[ 2 ]. However, replication studies have not confirmed these findings[ 3 ]. The role of the XbaI ESR1 polymorphism rs9340799 in AIS has never been described in Caucasian AIS patients.
blind_target.outcome_quote: No association between ESR1 XbaI polymorphism and AIS was found in the Caucasian population. None of the previously reported associations with curve severity, progression or operation rate could be confirmed.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract tests the previously reported ESR1 XbaI associations in a new Caucasian sample and explicitly states that no association was found and none of the prior associations could be confirmed.

luna_triage.reason: The abstract reports a new Caucasian sample and directly tests AIS susceptibility and progression outcomes for the ESR1 XbaI polymorphism. It concludes that none of the previously reported associations could be confirmed. Wu et al. (2006) is the supplied source reference whose title identifies susceptibility to AIS; the only supplied shipped original is Inoue et al. (2002), a distinct paper on curve severity. The specifically listed prior adjudication file was not present at its path, so no prior objection text was available to inspect.
luna_triage.location: Purpose, Methods, Results, Conclusions and discussion; References
luna_triage.omission_quote: There was no significant difference in alleles (p=0.63) and genotype frequency (p=0.35) between AIS patients (AA n=95, AG n=141, GG n=50) and controls (AA n=31, AG n=66, GG n=19).
